entities.summary: Nomus was a prominent Eastern Roman diplomat and statesman who served as the ambassador to the Western Roman Empire from 410 CE to 455 CE. He was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Callinicus, which ended the Roman-Saxon War and established a temporary peace between the two powers. Nomus's diplomatic efforts were marked by his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Eastern and Western Roman Empires, as well as his efforts to strengthen the Eastern Roman economy and trade networks. His leadership played a crucial role in maintaining stability in the region during a time of great turmoil. The Treaty of Callinicus was a significant achievement that showcased Nomus's skill as a diplomat and his commitment to peace and cooperation. Despite his efforts, the Western Roman Empire would eventually decline and fall, but Nomus's legacy as a diplomat and statesman endured. He is remembered as a key figure in the history of the Eastern Roman Empire and a champion of peace and cooperation in a time of great need. Nomus's diplomatic career was also marked by his efforts to promote the interests of the Eastern Roman Empire and its people, particularly in the areas of trade and commerce.
